changes.name: numpy.genfromtxt
changes.old: (fname, dtype=, comments=, delimiter=, skiprows=, usecols=, unpack=, ndmin=)
changes.new: (fname, dtype=, comments=, delimiter=, skip_header=, skip_footer=, converters=, missing_values=, filling_values=, usecols=, names=, excludelist=, deletechars=, replace_space=, autostrip=, case_sensitive=, defaultfmt=, unpack=, usemask=, loose=, invalid_raise=, max_rows=, encoding=, *, ndmin=, like=)
changes.reason: NumPy's own genfromtxt signature (NumPy 2.5). The recorded one was loadtxt's: genfromtxt was an alias of loadtxt, and skiprows was never a genfromtxt parameter of NumPy's.

changes.name: matplotlib.pyplot.Axes.annotate
changes.old: (self, text, xy, xytext=, arrowprops=, fontsize=, ha=, **kw=)
changes.new: (self, text, xy, xytext=, xycoords=, textcoords=, arrowprops=, annotation_clip=, **kw=)
changes.reason: Matplotlib's own annotate signature (3.11.1): xycoords, textcoords and annotation_clip are its parameters, xycoords the fourth; the recorded order put arrowprops fourth, where Matplotlib reads a positional argument as xycoords. ha and fontsize are read from **kwargs, as Matplotlib's Text keywords are: a ninth positional argument is refused, as in Matplotlib.

changes.name: pathlib.PureWindowsPath.ntpath
changes.reason: Upstream removed it: 3.14.4's PureWindowsPath class body did `import ntpath`, so the module was a class attribute; 3.14.10's pathlib imports ntpath at module level (pathlib.ntpath). Checked: hasattr(pathlib.PureWindowsPath, 'ntpath'), hasattr(pathlib.WindowsPath, 'ntpath') on CPython 3.14.4: True, True; on CPython 3.14.10: False, False. P3b-1's resync of pathlib to 3.14.10 follows it.

changes.name: sage_all.LaurentSeriesRing
changes.reason: Sage 10.10's own LaurentSeriesRing signature, from the oracle's inspect.signature: (base_ring, name=None, arg2=None, names=None, sparse=False, default_prec=None, order=, num_gens=, implementation=). The third positional argument is arg2 (a default precision after one name, a count after several, a name string after a count), and default_prec is a keyword of its own, so (QQ, 'x,y', default_prec=7) and (QQ, 2, names='x') read as Sage reads them (board's C1, daybreak3's SERIES-NAME-WORK-4). Positional calls keep their meaning.
